Draw two-channel colour tiles

Source: R/seq_tile_mix.R
seq_tile_mix.Rd

Draws one rectangle per row over [x0, x1] x [y_min, y_max]. Two intensities in [0, 1], a and b, set the colour: the hue is interpolated between color_a and color_b by b / (a + b) and the depth from white is max(a, b). Rows with both intensities zero or missing are not drawn. Tiles carry a hairline border in their own colour so adjacent tiles show no seams. Draw bound lines with seq_segment().

Usage

seq_tile_mix(
  data = NULL,
  mapping = NULL,
  aesthetics = aes(),
  legend = NULL,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A GRanges with one row per tile.

mapping

A SeqMap. Fields: x0 (default start), x1 (default end), y_min, y_max, a, b.

aesthetics

A SeqAes. Recognised: color_a (default "#D62728"), color_b (default "#2B59C3"), seam (border line width, default 0.25).

legend

NULL for the default 2D key from seq_legend_2d(), FALSE for no key, or a SeqLegend2DSpec used as given.

show_legend

Logical. FALSE suppresses the key.

...

Unused.

Value

A SeqTileMixR6 instance.

Examples

gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(c(1, 101), c(100, 200)),
  lo = c(0, 0.2), hi = c(0.2, 0.4), g = c(1, 0.5), l = c(0, 0.5))
seq_tile_mix(gr, map(y_min = lo, y_max = hi, a = g, b = l))
